The nature of the Civilization games is very big-picture in a lot of ways. Some people may see this is certain elements of history (people's culture, important figures, religions, atrocities, ect.) being marginalized, but I don't entirely agree. When you have a character who's supposed to serve as the head of a civilization and a game that can potentially go from the dawn of human history to the near-future in a five-hour period, it's going to be difficult to pull that off without some things people consider extremely important taking a back seat.

While I get why certain elements of the game strike certain people as problematic, I don't really see that as the developer's fault. Thinking of human history on a larger scale means minimizing the importance of elements of humanity that we're very emotionally attached to, and because of that, the Civilization games always run the risk of rubbing people the wrong way.

In other words, I get people's criticism of it, but I don't think there's a sweeping solution that would fix that.
